title: Haptic Handwheel — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Haptic Handwheel's rich face: three walks the Shop made on the steward's own feel engine (the struck spring measured against the pendulum, a stiff spring sent down a wire until the engine draws where every feel can live, and the knob with a light against the knob with a motor, ending on a note you land three ways), beside the steward's feel lab, his renders of four feels and his stability chart, with the fingerprint of the words each was made against. A screen can't push back, so every piece says what it can test and what only a hand can. I grow when the entry is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: 'Soft feels can cross a cable' holds only when the damping stays on the device or a hand holds the knob. On the steward's own engine and numbers, the softest feel on the page, the pitch-wheel return at 0.03 N·m/rad, grows with no hand on it over USB (4 ms assumed: its swing ×6.74 wider after 30 swings; the closed form's edge is 0.022 N·m/rad) and as an audio line (×25.8; edge 0.019). The steward's own verdict table (proofs/feel-lab/feel_lab_results.json) already marks it 'only while held' on both lanes. It crosses calmly with 0.002 N·m·s/rad of damping kept on the device (the steward's rescue: edge 0.48 over USB), with the motor's own back-EMF brake on at its lowest guess, or held. Possible wording: 'Soft feels can cross a cable, if the damping stays on the device.' The piece 'a stiff spring down a wire' shows it in its last two steps; checks.mjs re-runs it.

'A pendulum quickens as it settles' is true of a hard strike, and a light one hides it. On the steward's engine with the pretend motor's friction, from 2.3 rad (as far as the 0.2 N·m torque cap lets the 0.085 spring go) the pendulum climbs 4.61 → 5.78 Hz (+25%) while the spring holds 5.89 → 5.81 Hz (−1.4%); from 1 rad the pendulum climbs only +3.1%; from 0.5 rad not at all; and under about 0.3 rad friction stops either knob within a swing. The spring's 'one rate all the way down' holds to the last half swing or two, where sticking friction catches the knob and slows it 3 to 8%. Possible wording: 'a spring wobbles at one rate all the way down, and a pendulum, struck hard, quickens as it settles.' The piece 'the struck spring' measures it; checks.mjs re-runs it.

pieces.title: pitch you can lean on · frets, let go thirty-two times
pieces.caption: Four passes of eight let-gos, clicks marking the passes: no motor bumps, the motor's raw bumps, bumps cancelled, then bumps cancelled with the push off the ridge. Each landed note plays beside its in-tune neighbour, so slow beating means a sour landing. The steward's feel map measured the last pass landing within 2.4 cents every time. Rendered by the engine, not yet heard by an agent.
pieces.near: a spring wobbles at one rate all the way down

pieces.title: the lock · an LFO eased down to the beat
pieces.caption: The hand eases an LFO's rate down to the beat over eight seconds; the tremolo crawls against the clicks, then locks. Where each click landed in the wobble, as a fraction of its cycle, in the same run: 0.50, 0.99, 0.48, 0.01, 0.26, 0.50, 0.74, 0.98, 0.23 while it crawls, then 0.02, 0.01, 0.01, 0.00, 1.00, 1.00 … once locked: the same point every time. Not yet heard by an agent.
pieces.near: a spring wobbles at one rate all the way down

pieces.title: haptic filtering · the knob plays a melody
pieces.caption: The knob turns itself to each note of a melody, then a finger brakes it and the glides slow, then the hand grips it and adds vibrato. The sound follows where the knob actually is. Not yet heard by an agent.
pieces.near: a spring wobbles at one rate all the way down

pieces.title: the turntable · four ways to hold 33⅓
pieces.caption: A riff on the platter through one scene of braking and letting go, four times, one to four ticks marking each: the push alone, an ordinary speed correction (listen for the yelp after the drag), one that learns only near speed, and the final design, which knows the cost of spinning and trims. The steward notes he hasn't listened to it either.
pieces.near: a spring wobbles at one rate all the way down

pieces.file: Haptic Handwheel — rich — the struck spring.html
pieces.title: the struck spring · a walk in four steps
pieces.caption: **Does a spring wobble at one rate all the way down, and does a pendulum quicken?** Strike a spring, then a pendulum, put a finger on it, then strike both from one pull and read the rates the engine measures. From 2.3 rad on the pretend motor the spring holds 5.89 → 5.81 Hz and the pendulum climbs 4.61 → 5.78 Hz; from a small pull they can't be told apart. Sound after a click.
pieces.near: a spring wobbles at one rate all the way down

pieces.title: the feel lab · every feel, dragged
pieces.caption: The steward's lab: the seven feels on one simulated knob you drag, with the motor's brake and bumps switchable and the feel map's table. The pieces on this face run the same engine, inlined unchanged. Its own notes box is the steward's; nothing typed there is kept.
pieces.near: Here the disturbance is the playing

pieces.title: how stiff before delay makes it buzz · the steward's sweep
pieces.caption: The stiffest spring that stays calm on each lane, hands off (bright) and gripped (dim), on a log scale, with the stiffness each feel needs as numbered lines. Simulated with assumed numbers; it matches the closed form within about 10%. The walk beside it draws the same edge cell by cell.
pieces.near: delay makes a stiff spring unstable

pieces.file: Haptic Handwheel — rich — a stiff spring down a wire.html
pieces.title: a stiff spring down a wire · a walk in five steps
pieces.caption: **Is a stiff feel only safe near the motor, and can a soft one cross a cable?** One spring on the motor, then down a wire, then held, then with damping kept on the device; last, the engine draws stiffness against delay and runs every feel on every lane. The stiff feels need the motor. The softest feel crosses a cable only with damping kept local or a hand on it. Silent.
pieces.near: delay makes a stiff spring unstable

pieces.file: Haptic Handwheel — rich — two parts or one.html
pieces.title: two parts or one · a walk in four steps
pieces.caption: **Does the news come back through the part already in the hand?** A plain knob, then a light beside it (two parts), then one motor that senses and pushes, then the test: land nine named notes, three ways, and see where your eyes had to be. On the engine, a motor knob let go within 45 cents of a note lands on it within 2 cents every time; a plain knob stays wherever it was let go. A screen can't push back, so this tests where the news lives, not whether a hand feels it. Sound after a click.
pieces.near: Here the motor both senses and pushes
